stories.title: Azacitidine mechanism re-evaluated
stories.summary: Azacitidine has been a standard treatment for blood cancers for over two decades. While long thought to function by modifying DNA to reactivate silenced genes, new research suggests the drug acts primarily on RNA. The drug has been working, just not in the way previously assumed.

stories.title: Researchers model thoracic surgery adhesions
stories.summary: Intrathoracic adhesions often complicate repeat surgeries, yet their molecular origins remain poorly understood. A Japanese research team has developed an animal model to replicate these pleural adhesions. They aim to identify the specific cells and signaling pathways responsible for the formation of the internal scar tissue.

stories.title: Daraxonrasib shows promise in pancreatic cancer trial
stories.summary: A combination of daraxonrasib and chemotherapy resulted in substantial tumor shrinkage for patients with metastatic pancreatic cancer. These findings come from a Phase I/II clinical trial. The treatment is intended for cancer that has already spread to other parts of the body.

stories.title: Genetic blueprint of immune aging identified
stories.summary: A Monash University study has mapped the genetic changes that cause immune cells to lose effectiveness with age. Published in Science Immunology, the research suggests these shifts explain why older populations face higher risks of cancer and infection. The body has a blueprint for its own decline.

stories.title: Protein positioning linked to childhood epilepsy
stories.summary: University of Liverpool scientists have identified the specific positioning of a protein within nerve cells associated with a severe form of childhood epilepsy. The discovery provides new insight into the mechanics of this rare genetic neurological disorder. The protein has a designated place in the cell.

stories.title: Inner ear study challenges hearing mechanics
stories.summary: New research proposes a revised understanding of how the inner ear processes sound. The findings could eventually influence the development of hearing technologies such as cochlear implants. The ear has been doing things differently than previously thought.

stories.title: MRI tool aims to track pancreatic cancer treatment
stories.summary: Many pancreatic cancer patients are ineligible for surgery due to advanced disease and must rely on chemotherapy to shrink tumors. A new clinical trial at The Ohio State University is testing an MRI tool designed to determine the effectiveness of this treatment within weeks.

stories.title: Antibody drug shows early results in sarcoma trial
stories.summary: An antibody-drug conjugate has shown early potential in treating diverse soft tissue sarcomas during a phase I trial. The drug is designed to enter cancer cells like a Trojan Horse. Fewer than one in five patients with metastatic sarcoma survive five years.

stories.title: Mavenclad study tracks cognitive function in MS patients
stories.summary: A study of 280 patients found that those treated with Mavenclad maintained cognitive function over four years. The therapy was also linked to reduced relapses and improved quality of life. The drug appears to sustain control of inflammatory disease activity in relapsing multiple sclerosis.

stories.title: JAK inhibitor trial targets Down syndrome inflammation
stories.summary: A phase 2 trial found that tofacitinib, a JAK inhibitor, reduced inflammation in people with Down syndrome. The study, published in Cell Reports Medicine, also noted improvements in inflammatory skin conditions. The drug is now being explored for its potential impact on brain health.

stories.title: Engineered bacteria improve metabolism in aged mice
stories.summary: Researchers identified gut microbiome changes linked to human longevity and replicated them in aged mice using engineered bacteria. The study, published in Cell Metabolism, suggests these age-related microbial shifts may be protective adaptations. The gut is being asked to act younger than it is.

stories.title: Blood test measures Alzheimer's protein tangles
stories.summary: A new blood test from Alamar Biosciences measures eMTBR-tau levels to track the accumulation of tau protein tangles in the brain. Researchers presented the findings at the Clinical Trials on Alzheimer's Disease conference. The test aims to quantify the progression of the disease.

stories.title: India reaches 80 lakh HPV vaccinations
stories.summary: The Union Ministry of Health and Family Welfare announced that India has surpassed 80 lakh HPV vaccinations. The government describes the milestone as a step toward strengthening preventive healthcare. The campaign focuses on protecting against HPV infections and associated cancers.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat World’s Largest Public Healthcare Scheme, Covers 60 Crore+ Beneficiaries: PM Narendra Modi - DD News
Health Ministry proposes antimicrobial regulation
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has proposed including antimicrobials in the definition of new drugs under the 2019 rules. The amendment aims to increase regulatory scrutiny for manufacturing licenses. The move follows concerns regarding the lack of stability and bioequivalence studies for current antimicrobial products.

stories.title: NMC urges colleges to join PM-RAHAT scheme
stories.summary: The National Medical Commission has requested that all government medical colleges onboard the PM-RAHAT scheme. The initiative provides cashless emergency treatment for road accident victims. The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is seeking to expand the reach of the emergency care program.

stories.title: Karnataka launches antimicrobial resistance action plan
stories.summary: The Karnataka Department of Health and Family Welfare has launched a state action plan to contain antimicrobial resistance. The initiative focuses on surveillance, infection control, and antimicrobial stewardship. The plan aims to address the growing threat of resistance through a One Health collaboration.

stories.title: Ayushman Bharat scheme marks eight years
stories.summary: The Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY scheme has completed eight years, funding 13.25 crore hospital admissions. As of September 2026, 48.51 crore people hold cards under the program. The government reports that treatment worth Rs 2.03 lakh crore has been provided to economically vulnerable families.

stories.title: Government monitors Ebola outbreak in Central Africa
stories.summary: The Ministry of Health and Family Welfare is monitoring an Ebola outbreak in parts of the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda. The World Health Organization has declared a Public Health Emergency of International Concern. Indian health officials have initiated precautionary measures to address the evolving situation.

stories.title: AIIMS Bhubaneswar adds robotic surgery and liver transplant units
stories.summary: Union Health Minister Jagat Prakash Nadda inaugurated a new liver transplant unit and a surgical robotic system at AIIMS Bhubaneswar. The minister described the launch of an indigenous Tetanus and Adult Diphtheria vaccine as a move to strengthen national health security and achieve self-reliance in pharmaceuticals.

stories.title: Centre proposes tighter oversight for antimicrobial drugs
stories.summary: The government has proposed bringing antimicrobials under the regulatory framework used for new drugs. The Health Ministry aims to address concerns regarding manufacturing licences granted without adequate scrutiny, including the absence of required bioavailability and stability studies. The proposal was issued via a draft gazette notification.

stories.title: Health Ministry seeks to classify antimicrobials as new drugs
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has proposed amending the New Drugs and Clinical Trials Rules to include antimicrobials in the definition of new drugs. The move aims to strengthen regulatory oversight and address antimicrobial resistance, a priority underscored by the G20 New Delhi Leaders Declaration.

stories.title: ICMR report finds rising antibiotic resistance in India
stories.summary: A new ICMR report indicates that common antibiotics are losing effectiveness against bacteria responsible for urinary and bloodstream infections. Laboratory tests show high resistance to drugs like cefotaxime and ciprofloxacin. Treatment options are shrinking as drug resistance continues to spread across hospitals in India.

stories.title: Health Ministry marks World AMR Awareness Week
stories.summary: The Union Health Ministry has inaugurated World Antimicrobial Resistance Awareness Week, highlighting the misuse of medicines as a major public health challenge. Officials warned that overuse is reducing the effectiveness of treatments, potentially making common infections difficult to manage and undermining decades of medical progress.

stories.title: Study finds low-quality RSV information on TikTok
stories.summary: A study published in Vaccine examined TikTok videos regarding respiratory syncytial virus prevention, including maternal vaccines and infant antibodies. Researchers found that only 47 percent of the content presented high-quality information. Many people currently rely on social media platforms to learn about health trends.

stories.title: WHO warns of smoking impact on fertility
stories.summary: The World Health Organization has issued a report warning that smoking cigarettes may lower the odds of having a child. The health agency stated that the risk applies to both women and men.

stories.title: Measles cases surge as vaccination rates fall
stories.summary: The United States, Mexico, and Bolivia have lost their measles-free status, joining a list of nations where the infection has returned. International health officials noted that falling vaccination rates are leaving children vulnerable to the virus. Measles can trigger pneumonia and cause severe respiratory distress.

stories.title: South Korea reports first cholera case in a decade
stories.summary: South Korea has confirmed its first cholera case in ten years. Health authorities are tracing the source of the infection after a patient in Changwon tested positive. The individual, who has since recovered, reported no recent international travel. Officials are urging the public to use safe water.

stories.title: Palestinian Health Ministry reports deaths of children awaiting medical evacuation
stories.summary: The Palestinian Health Ministry stated that at least 300 children have died while waiting for authorization to leave the Gaza Strip for medical treatment. Another 5,400 children remain on evacuation lists. The ministry warned that delays and restrictions are placing those requiring specialized care at immediate risk.

stories.title: Surgeon calls for investigation into Scottish hospital deaths
stories.summary: A consultant surgeon has called for a police investigation into Aberdeen Royal Infirmary following reports of at least 19 patient deaths from avoidable surgical complications. The surgeon alleged that senior officials at NHS Grampian failed to act on repeated warnings about liver and pancreatic surgery standards.

stories.title: Health Ministry issues warning after rabid dog found in playground
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has requested that anyone who came into contact with a rabid American Bully dog in a Kfar Ruth playground between August 26 and 27 contact their local health bureau. A woman in her 30s was hospitalized in critical condition following the incident.

stories.title: Inquiry finds UK border failures during pandemic
stories.summary: A government inquiry concluded that the lack of international border controls left the UK extremely vulnerable at the start of the Covid-19 pandemic. The report stated that failures to implement test-and-trace systems allowed the virus to spread unchecked. The country was described as woefully ill-prepared.

stories.title: India misses 2025 tuberculosis elimination target
stories.summary: India fell short of its national target to eliminate tuberculosis by 2025. While the mortality rate dropped by 38 percent since 2015, the country still accounts for nearly a quarter of the global TB burden. WHO figures for 2025 incidence are currently under review.

stories.title: Latvia proposes raising alcohol purchasing age
stories.summary: Latvia's Health Ministry has proposed raising the minimum age for purchasing alcohol from 18 to 20 by 2028. The plan includes a total ban on alcohol advertising and a prohibition on sales at petrol stations. The government is currently reviewing the impact of these potential restrictions.

stories.title: Health Ministry advises on antibiotic use for children
stories.summary: The Health Ministry has urged parents to use antibiotics responsibly, noting that they do not treat viral infections like colds or flu. Misuse contributes to antimicrobial resistance, which the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control links to over 35,000 deaths annually in the EU.

stories.title: US loses measles elimination status
stories.summary: The Pan American Health Organisation has revoked the measles elimination status of the United States after 26 years. Over 5,400 cases were reported in 2026, the highest total since 1991. Data indicates that 96 percent of cases occurred in unvaccinated individuals or those with unknown status.

stories.title: ICMR mental health platform wins e-governance award
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has received a Gold Award at the National Awards for e-Governance 2026. The honour recognises the ICMR-MINDS platform for its innovative use of artificial intelligence to improve access to mental healthcare and strengthen citizen-centric service delivery across the country.

stories.title: ICMR reaches 100 technology transfers
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has reached 100 technology transfers, marking progress in translating indigenous health research into practical healthcare solutions. The milestone was announced at the third DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit in New Delhi, which hosted more than 600 participants.

stories.title: AIIMS faculty can now launch start-ups
stories.summary: AIIMS New Delhi has introduced a Faculty Entrepreneurship Policy allowing doctors and scientists to establish start-ups based on their research and clinical innovations. The institute proposes a 5 per cent non-dilutable equity stake in these ventures, aiming to turn academic work into commercially viable healthcare products.

Spain's Wilco raises €2.5M for AI that keeps clinic patients from dropping off - Dealroom
ICMR hits 100 technology transfer milestone
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has completed 100 technology transfer deals, including 20 licensing agreements. The milestone was disclosed at the third DHR-ICMR Health Research Excellence Summit in New Delhi, where officials highlighted the translation of domestic health research into usable technologies for public application.

stories.title: Luminopia wins digital health award at HLTH USA
stories.summary: Luminopia has been named a winner at the 2026 Digital Health Hub awards in Las Vegas. The company, which develops treatments for neuro-visual disorders, received the recognition in the Therapeutics, Pharmacy and Medication Innovation category during the annual HLTH USA event.

stories.title: ICMR launches biomedical innovation platform
stories.summary: The Indian Council of Medical Research has launched the Medical Innovations Patent Mitra platform to facilitate technology transfers to industry. The initiative aims to accelerate the commercialisation of indigenous healthcare technologies, with officials marking the event as a significant step for biomedical innovation in India.

stories.title: India expands AI use in healthcare
stories.summary: The Indian government is increasing the use of artificial intelligence to improve medical service delivery, citing gains in disease detection and telemedicine. Official data indicates that AI-enabled tools integrated into the National TB Elimination Programme have contributed to a 27 per cent decline in adverse outcomes.

stories.title: Cabo Verde joins Africa Health Data Forum
stories.summary: Cabo Verde participated in the first Africa Health Data Forum in Nairobi to discuss strengthening health information systems. The event focused on accelerating data transformation and the responsible use of artificial intelligence, with participants reviewing national progress and strategies for improving health data across the continent.

stories.title: IntelliProve raises €2.7M to bring health monitoring from smartphones to humanoid robots - Tech.eu
Study links BFRBs to youth distress
stories.summary: Research indicates that body-focused repetitive behaviours like skin picking and nail biting are common among young people. The study found these habits are frequently associated with significant distress, particularly in individuals who also experience anxiety, depression or bullying.

stories.title: Alcohol and eating disorders often overlap
stories.summary: Some individuals skip meals while drinking to amplify the effects of alcohol or manage calorie intake. This practice, sometimes called drunkorexia, highlights the crossover between risky alcohol consumption and disordered eating behaviours.

stories.title: Climate change impacts youth mental health in Colombia
stories.summary: A study of young people in Colombia’s Aburrá Valley found that 90 per cent want to take action against environmental degradation. Participants reported feelings of sadness, fear, powerlessness and guilt regarding the future, citing climate change as a primary source of their mental health distress.

stories.title: Children prefer family support for mental health
stories.summary: The EmpowerME project, involving 1,135 pupils, found that children view family and trusted adults as their primary source of mental health support. The research suggests children understand mental health through everyday experiences and value safe environments when facing difficulties.

stories.title: Consistency in exercise linked to mental well-being
stories.summary: A study of over 10,000 college students suggests that regular exercise may be more important for mental health than high-intensity workouts. Students who exercised less frequently were more likely to report anxiety and depression a year later, indicating that consistency is a key factor.

stories.title: NHS therapy access linked to workforce participation
stories.summary: A retrospective analysis of over half a million residents in England found a link between the availability of NHS primary care psychological therapies and workforce engagement. Regions providing a higher volume of appointments saw a narrowing of the employment gap for people with long-term mental health conditions.

stories.title: Researchers work with teenagers to address rising suicide rates
stories.summary: Teenagers at UC Berkeley are helping researchers design programs to address suicide rates among Black youth. Data shows the suicide rate for Black children aged 10 to 17 rose 144 percent between 2007 and 2020. The group is now looking for solutions to a persistent public health crisis.

stories.title: Focused ultrasound tested as treatment for chronic delusions
stories.summary: A pilot study published in npj Acoustics suggests low intensity ultrasound waves may temporarily reduce delusion severity in adults with chronic psychosis. Ten outpatients received the noninvasive treatment in a randomized trial. The study reports no serious side effects, though the research remains in the preliminary stages.

stories.title: Impact of social media restrictions on young people’s mental health goes under the spotlight - Cardiff University
UK study to track impact of planned social media ban
stories.summary: Researchers will track 300,000 young people in the United Kingdom to measure how a planned social media ban for under-16s affects mental health. Ten projects across England, Wales and Scotland will monitor phone habits ahead of the government restrictions scheduled to begin in the spring of 2027.

stories.title: Mental health crisis in children is real, say experts as cases soar fourfold - Medical Xpress
King's College London links climate change to mental health
stories.summary: Climate change is increasingly recognized as a major global health challenge, yet its impact on mental health remains poorly documented. Researchers at King's College London argue that exposure to extreme temperatures and flooding is linked to adverse mental health outcomes, requiring attention at the upcoming COP31 summit.

research.title: Experimental compound burns fat without sacrificing muscle
research.summary: Researchers at UC Berkeley have identified a compound that could transform weight-loss treatment by helping the body burn more energy instead of suppressing appetite like Ozempic and Wegovy. In mice, the compound boosted energy expenditure by up to 18%, improved blood sugar control, reduced liver fat, and promoted.

research.title: Keto diet slashes liver fat by 67% in just 4 months
research.summary: A new clinical trial found that the ketogenic diet dramatically outperformed Mediterranean and low-fat diets in reducing liver fat and improving metabolic health, even when participants lost similar amounts of weight. After just four to five months, about half of those following keto no longer met the criteria.

research.title: Powerful new weight-loss drug helps patients cut knee pain in half
research.summary: A powerful experimental weight-loss drug helped people with knee osteoarthritis lose about 25% of their body weight at the highest dose, while roughly two-thirds experienced at least a 50% reduction in knee pain. research.summary: Reading for pleasure may have surprisingly powerful benefits for the brain, with studies linking it to better memory, reduced stress, improved mental health, and a lower risk of dementia.
